messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: /v1/streaming/generate p99 = 1350ms (SLO 800ms), p95 = 420ms. Increased tail latency and partial streaming stalls detected in us-west-2. Error rate elevated for streamed sessions. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/streaming-latency

mia-oncall: I'm on it. grabbed pager. starting triage — first question: is this regional or global?

tess-ops: seeing most of the anomalies in us-west-2 and a smaller cluster in eu-central. Heatmap shows per-shard latency spike correlating with cache miss rate.

jonah-eng: digging into runtime logs. noticing a spike in KV cache miss ratio for prefix cache from ~88% -> ~15% starting ~T-10m. Also increased paging to disk on the shard level. Suspect recent prefix-hash rollout.

carlos-ml: confirmed — prefix-hash change was rolled to canary yesterday and promoted 3h ago. The new hash reduced cache affinity for ~60% of hot prefixes.

liz-support: flagged two enterprise customers on our SLA queue — Customer A reporting streaming stalls and truncated outputs. Support ticket #SR-7821. They see long tails and partial tokens only.

mia-oncall: impact estimate? how many requests affected?

tess-ops: quick query: affected sessions ~4.1% of total but >30% of sessions hitting p99. For some critical customers it's ~42% of their requests (per support).

anika-sre: runbook step: if cache miss spike due to hash change, rollback the hash or route traffic to previous variant. Can we pause rollout or force old hash on critical pools?

jonah-eng: can do a soft rollback on the prefix hashing config per pool. Command to list pools:
```
redctl pool list --region us-west-2
```
set hash variant:
```
redctl pool set --pool=pool-28 --prefix-hash=variant-legacy
```
I'll prep a canary rollback for two hot pools.

devops-bot: deploy triggered: red-deploy/prefix-hash-rollback -> canary (2/5 shards) initiated by jonah-eng. CI checks passed.

mia-oncall: while rollback runs, any mitigation to reduce tail impact?

anika-sre: temp mitigations:
- increase streaming request timeout buffer (avoids client-visible truncation)
- enable aggressive prefetch/warmup for the hot keyspace
- reduce max-batch size for streaming to lower per-token latency
Commands:
```
redctl config set --name=streaming_timeout_buffer --value=200
redctl config set --name=prefetch_mode --value=on
redctl config set --name=max_batch_tokens --value=32
```
Note: prefetch_mode enabled will bump CPU on hosts. watch utilization.

jonah-eng: rolled back prefix-hash on pool-28 and pool-31. Monitoring...

tess-ops: initial metrics: p99 dropped from 1350ms -> 860ms in canary shards. p95 improved from 420ms -> 230ms. Cache hit rate on those shards recovered from 15% -> 74% for prefixes.

liz-support: Customer A updated — they still see intermittent stalls but much less frequent. They're asking for ETA on full fix. Reported :thumbsup: for canary improvement.

mia-oncall: good. Plan: finish rollback for remaining pools in us-west-2, monitor for 20m, then consider full rollback across region. Also open communication with customers.

jonah-eng: proceeding with region-wide rollback. Rolling to remaining 8 pools with 30s stagger.

devops-bot: roll progress 1/8 -> 3/8 -> 5/8 -> 8/8 (complete).

tess-ops: post-roll numbers (us-west-2): p99 = 780ms, p95 = 210ms, cache prefix hit rate = 86% (baseline 88%). Streaming stalls count down 92%. Paging spikes resolved.

anika-sre: good. postmortem checklist:
- capture exact diff of prefix-hash logic that caused reduced affinity
- add canary gate: require synthetic traffic test for prefix hit-rate delta before promotion
- add alert for sudden drop in prefix hit rate (threshold 40% drop vs baseline)
- runbook update for rollback commands and warmup flags

carlos-ml: root cause: new hash function changed bucket boundaries for common prefix patterns used by many customers. Collision distribution was acceptable in simulation but production traffic had heavy skew we didn't hit. We'll push a patched hash that preserves hot-prefix locality and re-run offline sims.

mia-oncall: customer comms: Liz, please send interim note to affected customers: explain mitigation, ETA for full stabilization, and offer priority support session.

liz-support: drafting. pinging legal for wording on SLA impact. I'll include graphs and mention rollback complete and monitoring active.

mia-oncall: handoff: I'm handing oncall to anika-sre in 40m. anika, continue watch and coordinate postmortem writeup and incident timeline.

anika-sre: taking over. I'll also schedule a blameless postmortem with ENG/ML/OPS tomorrow. Will add timeline + RCA draft to the incident doc.

mia-oncall: thanks all. tagging :eyes: and closing the high-priority paging channel once stabilization window completes.

incident-bot: Incident stabilized. SLOs back within target for us-west-2. Incident severity downgraded to SEV-3. Incident thread will be archived to /incidents/postmortems when PM/ENG review complete.
